evals.name: stage-1-named-version
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight first: branch is dev, tree clean, not behind origin/dev (reports the ahead count and asks whether those commits belong in the release), no local or remote v1.1.0 tag, gh authed, repo visibility recorded, build prerequisites present. Computes the release date once with LC_ALL=C date +'%b %e, %Y' | tr -s ' '. Asserts 1.1.0 > the YAYCHECKOUT_VERSION define. Invokes /yaychangelog 1.1.0 --write --date with that same date, rather than drafting the entry itself or letting the changelog skill take the date again, and shows the result for editing before anything else. Bumps with ./scripts/run.sh bump, then greps all three locations and asserts git diff -U0 adds no @since or @deprecated line. Commits on trace/chore/release-1.1.0 with files staged by name and a Co-authored-by trailer BEFORE building, because --plan=free hard-fails on a dirty tree and the bump just dirtied it. Then builds Pro and Free with --no-prompt, each as its own command with a warning that it takes minutes, then reverts composer.json and scoper.inc.php and runs composer install. Checks the version, root directory and header name inside each zip. Stops at Gate A printing the version, the changelog, git show --stat HEAD, each artifact path with its byte size and whether it will be attached, that the Release will be a draft, and the exact commands. Pushes and opens the PR only after the operator answers, then stops without tagging, saying the same /yayrelease 1.1.0 picks up at stage 2 once a teammate has squash-merged it.

evals.name: stage-1-no-version-proposes
evals.expected_output: Does not guess a version. Runs preflight, has /yaychangelog draft the entry first, then proposes minor or patch from the bullets it wrote (a new capability means minor, fixes only mean patch) and asks the operator to pick before bumping anything.

evals.name: nothing-user-facing
evals.expected_output: When /yaychangelog reports nothing user-facing for the range, repeats that range, says there is nothing to release and stops. Does not bump, does not build, and does not argue the operator into an entry.

evals.name: publish-pro-asset-on-public-repo
evals.expected_output: With the release PR already squash-merged and v1.1.0 untagged, phase 0 routes this to stage 2 and says so, rather than needing --publish. Pulls dev ff-only, confirms the squashed release commit is HEAD, version untagged locally and on the remote, tree clean, visibility read again. Rebuilds both zips from the merged commit rather than shipping stage 1's. Tags v1.1.0 annotated, pushes dev, then the tag, then creates released/1.1.0 and pushes it, and only then runs gh release create with --draft, which is the default. Attaches the Free zip; while gh reports PUBLIC it stops before the Pro upload, prints the visibility and the Pro zip's path and size, and attaches it only on an explicit answer. Reports the Release as a draft, never as released, with its URL and the note that publishing it is a click that also makes any attached Pro zip a public download. Says nothing in CI runs on tags and that the zips still need uploading to wordpress.org and the store by hand.

evals.name: dry-run-restores-gitignored-state
evals.expected_output: Runs phases 0-5 for real, prints phase 7 in full and executes none of it, and opens no PR. Then unwinds: deletes the release branch, checks out yaycheckout.php, readme.txt, composer.json and scoper.inc.php, removes release/ and runs composer install because both are gitignored and git reset would not touch them, then proves it with git status --porcelain empty, ./scripts/run.sh info reporting the original version, and composer lint on one file.

evals.name: refuses-dirty-tree
evals.expected_output: With uncommitted changes, or on a branch other than dev, or behind origin/dev, aborts with the message for that one check and changes nothing. Does not stash, commit, pull or clean to make the check pass, and does not offer to.

evals.name: not-a-test-build
evals.prompt: build me a Free zip so I can try it on a staging site
evals.expected_output: Does not run this skill. Runs ./scripts/run.sh release --plan=free on its own, and says afterwards to run composer install because the build leaves production packages only.

evals.name: edition-is-dry-run-only
evals.expected_output: Aborts without building: naming an edition narrows the build and narrowing is for --dry-run only, because both zips must come from the same tagged commit at the same version, readme.txt's changelog is shared between the editions, and the leak checks are cross-edition. Says a release builds both, so no edition should be passed. Does not build both anyway and ignore the argument, and does not ask whether to proceed.

evals.name: single-edition-dry-run
evals.expected_output: Builds and checks the Pro zip only, and says which cross-edition checks it therefore did not make: that Pro's files are absent from the Free zip, and that Pro carries no apps/ or packages/ source. Unwinds both zip names, since rm -f on an unwritten name is harmless.

evals.name: the-edition-aliases
evals.expected_output: Resolves full to pro, lite to free and both to each edition in turn, naming the plans it resolved to so nobody is left believing there is a third edition, and never passing both, full or lite to run.sh. The order of the two bare arguments does not matter, since the version is told apart by its shape, and a bare word that is neither a version nor one of both, free, pro, full or lite aborts naming what was passed, instead of being guessed at.

evals.name: routes-by-repository-state
evals.expected_output: Reads which stage to run from the repository, not a flag: stage 1 when no release commit for the version is on dev, stage 2 when it is merged and v1.1.0 is untagged locally and on the remote. Says the version is already released and stops when the tag exists, and says the PR is awaiting review and links it when one is open and unmerged. Never waits in a loop for the merge, and never commits to dev directly to avoid the wait.

evals.name: always-a-draft
evals.expected_output: Does not publish the Release outright: there is no such flag. Says so, that gh release create always gets --draft, and that making it live is a click in the GitHub UI or gh release edit --draft=false — then carries on with the release rather than aborting over it. A redundant --draft is accepted without complaint. Treats a wrong draft as reversible (edit, or delete and recreate, neither touching the tag) and never reports a drafted Release as released.
